history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. Roman Catholic basilica in Old Goa housing the tomb and mortal remains of St. Francis Xavier, Jesuit missionary and co-founder of the Society of Jesus (died 1552 off China; body brought to Goa 1554). Construction began 1594 under the Jesuits (designed by Domingos Fernandes; foundation laid under Philip I / Governor Francisco da Gama); consecrated May 1605 by Archbishop Dom Fr. Aleixo de Menezes. India's first Minor Basilica (1946); UNESCO World Heritage Site (1986) as part of the 'Churches and Convents of Goa'. Baroque church built of laterite; the only major Goan church never plastered (plaster removed 1956). The silver-casket mausoleum (1696) was a gift of Cosimo III de' Medici, Grand Duke of Tuscany. name: Basilica of Bom Jesus
town_description: Old Goa (Velha Goa), on the banks of the Mandovi river in Tiswadi taluka, was the capital of Portuguese India from the 16th century until its 18th-century decline. Its surviving churches and convents form a UNESCO World Heritage Site. About 10 km east of Panaji, it is the heart of Goa's Portuguese-era heritage.
